en.name: Frances Xavier Cabrini
en.summary: Italian nun who, redirected from her hoped-for missions in China, instead built an extensive network of institutions serving Italian immigrants in the Americas.
en.body: Frances Xavier Cabrini founded the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in Italy hoping to be sent as a missionary to China, but Pope Leo XIII redirected her toward the millions of Italian immigrants arriving in the United States, telling her "not to the East, but to the West." Arriving in New York in 1889 to find the promised support for her mission had fallen through, she nonetheless began founding schools, hospitals, and orphanages to serve impoverished Italian immigrant communities facing discrimination and neglect, eventually establishing dozens of institutions across the United States, Central and South America, and Europe despite a lifelong fear of water that never eased her many transatlantic crossings. She became a naturalized American citizen and built one of the largest networks of Catholic social institutions of her era. She died in Chicago in 1917 and was canonized in 1946, becoming the first United States citizen to be declared a saint.
